text:
olga_customer: hey, we're hitting weird rerank scores after moving to the new embed model. results are basically random — not just lower scores, they don't correlate with relevance at all. filing ticket #INC-9421. can someone triage?

jules_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the request payload (no secrets) and the models you used for embedding + rerank? quick Q: did you change the embed model recently? :eyes:

olga_customer: yeah we switched from `embed-large-384-v1` to `embed-lite-128-v2` last week to save cost. our flow: 1) call /v1/embeddings with embed-lite-128-v2, store vectors; 2) later call /v1/rerank with stored vectors + queries. payload looks like:```json
{
  "query": "How to reset my password?",
  "documents": [
    {"id":"doc1","embedding":[0.001, -0.12, ... /* 128 values */]},
    {"id":"doc2","embedding":[0.12, 0.03, ... ]}
  ],
  "reranker_model": "rerank-bert-384-v2"
}
```
we don't get an explicit error, just output scores that rank irrelevant docs higher.

kevin_support: thanks — that pattern screams dim mismatch. reranker expects a 384-dim vector but you're passing 128-dim vectors. server should've validated though. can you share a minimal repro (curl) and a truncated log showing the request/response?

olga_customer: here's a sanitized curl we used against the hosted endpoint:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"query":"reset password","documents":[{"id":"1","embedding":[0.0,0.1,...(128 numbers)]}],"model":"rerank-bert-384-v2"}'
```
and response:```json
{"results":[{"id":"1","score":0.98}],"note":"no error"}```

matt_repro: repro'ed locally with a small script. when I pass 128-d vectors to the reranker (which uses an internal matrix expecting 384) it currently does a zero-padding to 384 silently in the runtime and proceeds. padding produces degenerate inner products so scores become meaningless. this explains the random-looking order.

ingrid_eng-ml: tagging in. thanks for the repro notes — silent zero-pad is the problem. we have two orthogonal issues: (1) server-side validation is missing for embed dimension vs reranker expected dim, and (2) silent padding leads to misleading scores rather than an informative error. both are engineering/product issues.

ingrid_eng-ml: short-term mitigation options: 1) fail-fast with 400 + explicit message like `embedding dimension (128) incompatible with reranker (384)`; 2) server-side projection: run a learned/linear projection from 128->384 (but that's risky for quality); 3) docs/console warning for mix-and-match. my recommendation: implement fail-fast in hosted API and surface a migration guide.

jules_support: agree — please escalate to eng-ml for a fast fail. I'll notify the customer and add suggested repro steps. olga, we'll pause your prod rerank jobs while we fix to avoid bad UX. want to keep you on the thread for quick followups.

olga_customer: thanks — pausing is fine. would a service flag to auto-project be acceptable short-term? some of our workloads can tolerate projection.

ingrid_eng-ml: we'll need product signoff if we add auto-projection. it's not free (latency + quality risk). for now we'll: implement server-side validation + explicit 400 + a help link. then iterate on a projection feature gated behind a flag/opt-in for dedicated/private customers.

kevin_support: jotting down the exact error message text we want in the API: `400 Bad Request — embedding dimension 128 incompatible with rerank model rerank-bert-384-v2 (expected 384).` include a `compatibility_suggestion` field with "use embed-large-384-v1 or re-embed with a compatible model" or "enable projection: true".

matt_repro: added a minimal repro script to the thread:```python
# repro-rerank-dim-mismatch.py
import requests
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank'
payload = {
  'query':'reset',
  'model':'rerank-bert-384-v2',
  'documents':[{'id':'a','embedding':[0.0]*128}]
}
res = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer TOKEN'})
print(res.status_code, res.text)
```
works locally: returns 200 + weird scores. changing embedding to 384 dims returns sensible ranking.

ingrid_eng-ml: created internal issue ENG-ML-1287 to add validation and an informative error + unit tests. @deploy-bot can we get a quick patch to reject mismatched dims on hosted? :pray:

deploy-bot: staging deployment started for patch/ENG-ML-1287 (ci/build-4821). logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/4821 :construction_worker: 

kevin_support: i'll draft an outbound message to olga's team explaining root cause and ETA. Suggested wording in support ticket: "We detected an embedding dimension mismatch (128 vs 384). Our reranker runtime currently performs padding which resulted in inaccurate scores. We're rolling out a fix to validate and return an explicit error to prevent this. You can either re-run your embedding job with a 384-dim model or enable projection (coming soon)."

olga_customer: appreciated. can you include recommended re-embed commands? small one-liner would be great.

jules_support: sent to customer:```text
Hi Olga — quick update: root cause is mixing 128-dim embeddings with a 384-dim reranker. Temporary options: 1) re-embed with `embed-large-384-v1` (recommended), 2) downgrade reranker to `rerank-bert-128-compat` if you need immediate parity (if available), 3) wait for opt-in projection feature.
Re-embed example (python):
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key='...')
docs = load_docs()
vecs = [c.embeddings.create(model='embed-large-384-v1', input=d) for d in docs]
# store vecs and re-run rerank
```

ingrid_eng-ml: patch merged to staging. validation returns 400 with helpful JSON now. will promote to prod after 24h smoke tests.

deploy-bot: staging -> prod roll: queued. smoke tests scheduled.

kevin_support: updated ticket INC-9421 with root cause and next steps. ETA for prod rollout: ~48 hours. I'll keep you posted, @olga_customer.

olga_customer: thank you — appreciate the fast turnaround. we'll re-run a small batch re-embed tonight. please ping when prod rollout is done.

jules_support: closing loop for now. if you see any regressions after the re-embed or after prod rollout, please reopen. :thumbsup:
